state:
Goal `core-str-3-3`: `Core\Str::slice` has every feature proof on disk: description, three
examples, attack, bench record, a Rust test with its `covers:` marker, and a card in plain words.
`window` no longer counts the whole subject unless the length is negative, and a non-negative
length is walked from the start. `granularity::Unit::byte_of_index` reads only the prefix up to its
index, so a short slice at the start of a long text no longer scans all of it. Every `Core\Str` perf
record was re-measured after `str.rs` changed. The `Core\Queue::delete` attack has a 30 s limit:
it made about 25000 statements and ran past 10 s on a loaded machine; it takes about 4 s idle.
The members still owed in this goal are `split`, `startsWith`, `trim`, `trimStart`, `trimEnd`,
`wrap`, `upper` and `upperFirst`.

items.text: **`Core\Str::split`** — owes about, examples, hostile, perf, tests (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). Check whether it collects its parts outside the memory limit before it builds the array, as `reverse` did. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs:2049`

**`Core\Str::startsWith`** — owes about, examples, hostile, perf, tests (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`); a scalar result, so its bench declares `// bench: allocations 0`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs:1962`

**`Core\Str::trim`, `trimStart`, `trimEnd`** — each owes about, examples, hostile, perf, tests (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`); if the three share one implementation (not checked), one attack shape fits all three. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs:2301`

backlog: `Core\Str::wrap`, `upper`, `upperFirst` still owe every proof but help (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`).

`window` still counts the whole subject for a negative offset or length. `Unit::length_of` would read the cached grapheme count, but `window` gets `&str` and not the `Value` (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs` § `window`).
